The film follows communities located directly south of Francois Lake and tells the story of ordinary residents, First Nations and firefighters who chose flight over flight.. “At first it was not a film,” Tschanz said noting, he immigrated to Canada when he was 16 years old from Switzerland and his parents live in the area. At the time of the fires that resulted in ferry access being restricted, Tschanz was smuggled through the toxic smoke on a shipping boat with a friend. “It was just to document things and then create a GoFundMe page, and we had a video that would help people that had lost a lot in the community, but then what happened was the beautiful story of the community coming together and forming an organization.” That organization, Tschanz, said is the Chinook Emergency Response Society which is now a national blueprint on how smaller communities can be part of the solution when there is wildfire and they are too remote to access and provide resources and time. items.title: [cbc.ca] B.C. tribunal overturns $100,000 fine against X over intimate image
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

British Columbia’s Civil Resolution Tribunal has overturned a $100,000 penalty against social media platform X for failing to delete an intimate image posted without a woman’s consent, ruling that blocking access to it in Canada was a reasonable step under provincial law. The tribunal said the law did not make X liable after it blocked Canadian access to the image, which remained available outside Canada. The decision reversed a September 2025 penalty for failing to comply with an order to delete it. The tribunal accepted X’s argument that requiring worldwide removal could interfere with other countries’ legal systems and cited a 2024 Australian case as persuasive but not binding. Outgoing B.C. Attorney General Niki Sharma criticized X’s refusal to remove the image and said governments may need to strengthen laws or pursue legal action. The tribunal also rejected X’s request to require the complainant to pay more than US$100,000 in legal fees.

items.title: [thestar.com] Canada's elections chief warns AI chatbots can mislead voters
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Canada’s Chief Electoral Officer Stéphane Perrault warned members of Parliament that voters increasingly turn to AI chatbots rather than Elections Canada’s website for candidate information and voting instructions, sometimes receiving unreliable or incorrect answers. He said voters also lack a reliable way to determine whether information comes from a person or AI, who produced it, or what sources a chatbot used. Perrault called for mandatory labels on AI-generated election material and recommended that chatbots direct voting questions to official sources. items.title: [pbs.org] Greenland approves US defense pact, clearing path for expanded Arctic bases
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Greenland’s parliament voted 16-0 on Nov. 3, with seven lawmakers abstaining, to approve a security agreement with Denmark and the United States, clearing the way for expanded U.S. military access to the Arctic island. The pact permits two new U.S. defense sites and supports the Golden Dome missile-defense system while affirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. It would remain in force if Greenland later becomes independent. President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the agreement in September after Trump repeatedly pressed for U.S. control of Greenland and threatened force and tariffs against allies. Denmark has rejected a transfer of the territory but had been open to discussing a larger U.S. military presence. The Danish parliament is scheduled to take up the measure on Nov. 11 and vote on Nov. 19. The pact takes effect after the required Danish and Greenlandic parliamentary procedures and does not require U.S. Senate approval. Greenlandic officials and residents remain divided over whether the security arrangement brings tangible benefits to the island.

items.content_html:

Livestock guidance published across the United States, France and Poland focuses on forage stocks, grazing and feed transitions during drought and uneven feed supplies. In France, independent livestock nutrition consultant Eva Garre urged farmers to measure silage and hay reserves, account for losses of 15% to 30% and calculate shortages by date; early maize samples showed starch levels of 18 to 20 points, compared with the usual 34 to 37 in her region. Kenny Simon, an extension forages instructor at the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture, recommended rotational grazing, moving hay-feeding sites and planting winter annuals to reduce stress on dry pastures. A Polish cattle farm keeps cows and calves on about 100 hectares of pasture from May through November and produces its own hay and silage. South Dakota State University Extension feedlot specialist Warren Rusche advised keeping newly arrived calves in smaller feedlot pens for their first three weeks and feeding them twice daily during the initial adjustment. Argentine feedlot analyst Andrés Halle cautioned that theoretical feedlot margins can misstate results when current grain prices are applied to grain produced on-farm.

items.content_html:

The student-backed Student List is projected to win a majority in Serbia’s parliament after former President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in Sunday’s snap election, ending his Serbian Progressive Party’s 14-year dominance. Vučić said the list could take 135 to 140 of the 250 seats, against about 105 for his party; separate pollster projections put the Student List at 138 seats. The count remained preliminary. Turnout reached 67.6% by 7 p.m., the highest since Yugoslavia’s breakup in 1992. The election followed nearly two years of protests sparked by the November 2024 collapse of a railway-station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. Protesters blamed corruption and failures of oversight, accusations the government rejected. The movement’s anti-corruption campaign drew support beyond students, and it entered the election with a slate of civil society candidates. With final results still pending, the Student List faces the task of forming a government without a single established leader. Its candidates have limited political experience. European Union officials offered help with rule-of-law and media reforms, while Vučić alleged foreign interference without providing evidence.

The 2026-27 El Niño has strengthened across the tropical Pacific and is forecast to rank among the strongest on record, peaking during the Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter. The climate pattern increases the likelihood of drought in some regions and heavier rain in others, but does not determine local weather on its own. In the United States, forecasts point to warmer-than-average temperatures, wetter conditions in parts of the West and Southwest, and less rain and snow in the Pacific Northwest. California has already seen unusually high coastal water levels; a UC Davis report identifies low-lying roads, airports and neighborhoods at risk of flooding if high tides and winter storms coincide. Former officials and scientists warn that the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has lost roughly one-fifth of its staff since January 2025, weakening its forecasting and response capacity ahead of the season. New Zealand’s outlook for November 2026 through January 2027 points to a greater likelihood of dry conditions in the north and east of the North Island and heavier rain in the south and west of the South Island.

items.title: [cloud.google.com] Google bans Chinese partner after backdoor infects 1.3 million Android boxes
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Google and security partners disrupted the XCPE botnet, which had enrolled more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes. Google says it has high confidence that Shenzhen-based manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co. deliberately embedded the backdoor in device firmware and sold criminal groups access to infected hardware. The criminal groups used the devices to commit advertising fraud, route other people’s internet traffic through household connections and install additional malware. Google also reported that operators captured screens, collected account information and system logs, and issued commands remotely. The same malware appeared on telehealth equipment, karaoke machines and digital signs. Google’s takedown targeted XCPE control servers and domains used by more than a dozen related malware families. Google estimates the takedown could also cut criminal access to at least 10 million other devices compromised through separate routes. Videostrong evaded Google’s device checks by loading malicious code after a device’s first boot, Google said. Google has banned Videostrong and its future affiliates from making certified Android devices or supplying software to certified manufacturers, and says it changed its review process. The backdoor remains in affected devices and can reinstall after a reboot. Synthient, a security firm involved in the investigation, recommends disconnecting and replacing affected boxes.

The same malware appeared on telehealth equipment, karaoke machines and digital signs. Google’s takedown targeted XCPE control servers and domains used by more than a dozen related malware families. Google estimates the takedown could also cut criminal access to at least 10 million other devices compromised through separate routes (google.com, bleepingcomputer.com, helpnetsecurity.com). Videostrong evaded Google’s device checks by loading malicious code after a device’s first boot, Google said. Google has banned Videostrong and its future affiliates from making certified Android devices or supplying software to certified manufacturers, and says it changed its review process. The backdoor remains in affected devices and can reinstall after a reboot. Synthient, a security firm involved in the investigation, recommends disconnecting and replacing affected boxes (cyberscoop.com, thehackernews.com). Infection estimate: TrendAI counted 1,472,554 infected devices across 206 models between June 3 and Oct. 1, and said the actual total was at least that high (thehackernews.com). Global spread: Malaysia, Brazil, Iraq, Mexico and Taiwan had the largest concentrations; CyberScoop reported nearly 44,000 infected devices in the United States (cyberscoop.com, thehackernews.com). items.title: [sci.news] CERN experiment reports first evidence of ultra-rare beauty meson decay
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

The LHCb collaboration at CERN reported the first evidence of a neutral beauty meson (B⁰) decaying into two muons, a process predicted to occur about once in every 10 billion such particles. Combining the new result with earlier LHCb data gave the signal a statistical significance of 3.2 standard deviations—enough to count as evidence, but below the five-standard-deviation threshold for a discovery. The measured rate is consistent with the Standard Model, the leading theory of particle physics. Rare decays can be sensitive to effects from particles that are not produced directly in collisions. Researchers plan to continue collecting data into the early 2030s to refine the measurement; a further detector upgrade is also planned.
